subject: forensic-medicine
title: Heroin, Morphine, Naloxone and Opioid Overdose

steps.title: Heroin becomes morphine in the body
steps.tx: **Heroin**, diacetylmorphine or brown sugar, comes as white, brown and black tar forms, street names smack, junk and dope, diluted with quinine, lactose and mannitol, and combined with cocaine as speedballs. It is not taken orally because stomach hydrolysis destroys it; it is injected, heated on silver foil and inhaled as chasing the dragon, or snuffed. The body hydrolyses it to monoacetylmorphine then morphine within thirty to sixty minutes, so chemical analysis detects morphine but not heroin itself.
steps.say: Injected or smoked, never swallowed, heroin turns to morphine within the hour, which is all the laboratory ever finds.

steps.title: Overdose: the opioid triad
steps.tx: Opioid overdose is recognised by the **triad of respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils and depressed consciousness**, with a needle track, foam at the mouth and a syringe nearby completing the scene. Heroin causes sudden death even in long term users, sometimes with the needle still in the vein, from very strong central depressant action, personal hypersensitivity in a few, and alcohol aboard in almost all fatal cases. Intense euphoria lasts minutes, sedation about an hour, and effects are lost in three to six hours.
steps.say: Slow breathing, pinpoint pupils and coma with a fresh track are opioid overdose until naloxone proves it in minutes.

steps.tx: Opioid overdose is recognised by the **triad of respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils and depressed consciousness**. A fresh needle track, foam at the mouth, and a syringe nearby complete the scene. Heroin can kill suddenly even in a long term user, sometimes with the needle still in the vein, from intense central depression, rare personal hypersensitivity, and alcohol taken as well in almost every fatal case. Euphoria lasts minutes, sedation about an hour, and effects fade in three to six hours.
steps.say: Slow breathing, pinpoint pupils, and coma, plus a fresh track and a syringe, indicate opioid overdose. Heroin may kill at once, often with alcohol, even in a regular user, and the drug effect itself is largely gone within six hours.

vis.caption: Recent puncture marks and a nearby syringe mark the scene of injected opioid use. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Naloxone reverses the overdose
steps.tx: **Naloxone** is the narcotic antagonist that displaces opioids from their receptors and restores breathing within minutes, which is both treatment and diagnostic test. Because its action is shorter than heroin's sedation, the revived patient is observed for re sedation and the dose repeated or infused. For dependence treatment, naltrexone blocks euphoria, methadone forty milligrams daily usually prevents withdrawal and eighty blocks heroin euphoria, tapered by twenty percent daily, and addicts must never be handed twenty milligrams of methadone at one time outside supervision.
steps.say: Naloxone wakes the overdose in minutes but wears off first, so watch for the patient sinking back into sedation.

steps.title: Morphinism: the chronic addict
steps.tx: **Chronic morphine addiction** tolerance can reach three to six grams of opium daily. The addict shows dry skin, scars of healed abscesses and abscesses themselves and tattooing from needles. Pleasure gives way to disinterest and recurring depression, restlessness, irritability, disturbed sleep or insomnia, loss of memory, mental fatigue and gradual intellectual and moral deterioration, with constipation, contracted pupils, anorexia, emaciation, weakness and impotence. Sudden cessation in a dependent pregnant woman can endanger the fetus fatally.
steps.say: Needle scarred, constipated, emaciated and deteriorating describes morphinism, whose tolerance can reach grams a day.

steps.title: Withdrawal and methadone tapering
steps.tx: **Opioid withdrawal** in pethidine type dependence appears in three to four hours, peaks at eight to twelve and disappears in four to five days; morphine withdrawal runs a longer, miserable course of craving, lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, yawning, sweating, piloerection, diarrhoea and insomnia. Treatment is gradual withdrawal: methadone thirty to forty milligrams daily tapered off, dihydrocodeine or codeine for the less dependent, propranolol fifty milligrams against anxiety and craving, tranquillisers at bedtime and psychiatric counselling throughout.
steps.say: Tears, runny nose, yawning and diarrhoea mark withdrawal, answered by a slow methadone taper and counselling.

steps.title: Autopsy in heroin death
steps.tx: At **autopsy after heroin death** the lungs are heavy and congested with severe pulmonary oedema, the commonest finding, probably from sudden ventricular dysrhythmia, and microscopically show foreign body granulomas from injected adulterants. The liver shows chronic triaditis with mononuclear infiltrates. Morphine can sometimes be detected in liver or bile when none is detectable in blood or urine, and opiates are identifiable in hair, which also dates the habit. Fresh and old injection sites are photographed and excised for analysis.
steps.say: Heavy oedematous lungs with granulomas and a triaditis liver are heroin's autopsy signature, and bile may hold what blood lost.

steps.tx: After fatal heroin the lungs are heavy and congested with severe **pulmonary oedema**, the commonest autopsy finding, probably from a sudden ventricular dysrhythmia. Microscopy shows foreign body granulomas around injected adulterants, and the liver shows chronic triaditis with mononuclear infiltrates. Morphine may persist in liver or bile when blood and urine are negative, and opiates in hair can date the habit. Fresh and old injection sites are photographed and excised for analysis.
steps.say: Heroin death leaves heavy congested lungs full of oedema, most often after a sudden ventricular rhythm disturbance. Adulterants leave foreign body granulomas, and the liver shows chronic triaditis. Morphine may linger in bile or liver after blood and urine are negative, while hair dates the habit. Injection sites are photographed and sampled.

vis.caption: The lungs are heavy, wet and deeply congested, the usual internal finding when heroin has killed. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Pethidine, methadone and fentanyl relatives
steps.tx: The opioid family widens in **synthetic opioids**. Pethidine, fatal near two grams in twenty four hours, causes more dizziness and elation than morphine, incomplete tolerance with twitchings, tremors, confusion, hallucinations, dilated pupils and convulsions, addiction common among doctors and nurses, and dangerous reactions with monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Methadone is a long acting opioid of fifteen hour half life, more powerful than morphine. Fentanyl is fifty to one hundred times morphine's potency by vein, mouth, smoke, snort or skin patch.
steps.say: Pethidine addicts twitch and convulse among medical staff, methadone lasts fifteen hours, and fentanyl is a hundred times morphine.

steps.title: Barbiturates sit beside opioids in coma
steps.tx: **Barbiturates** are the other great depressant family: long acting onset two hours lasting six to twelve, intermediate half to one hour lasting three to six, short acting under three hours, and ultrashort pentothal acting immediately for five to ten minutes. Poisoning runs drowsiness and ataxia to deep coma with lost reflexes, reduced ventilation, cyanosis, hypotension and cold clammy skin. Barbiturates, alcohol and carbon monoxide can destroy the brain while the drug itself is fully excreted before death.
steps.say: Coma with lost reflexes and a cold clammy collapse may be barbiturate, and a negative level later never excludes it.

steps.title: Prescribing and custody duties with opioids
steps.tx: Opioids sit under the NDPS framework built earlier, and **opioid handling duties** bind the prescriber: prescription only supply, records of stock and administration, secure custody, and recognition that doctor and nurse addiction to pethidine is an occupational hazard needing treatment, not merely discipline. In overdose deaths the syringe, foil, powder residue and injection sites are seized with the body samples, because adulterants such as quinine in the powder can themselves contribute to death and to granulomas in the lungs.
steps.say: Records, locked custody and seized paraphernalia complete opioid care, and the powder's adulterants are evidence too.
